Subject: BlueHarbor Dedicated: prewarm matrix & burst crediting

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. As we discussed on the call, Blue Harbor's usage profile is spiky: heavy inference during 09:00-11:00 and 18:00-20:00 PT with unpredictable occasional batch jobs that can spike token throughput ~8-10x baseline for 10-30 minutes.

Attached is our week-by-week forecast for the next 6 months (summary tab + hourly heatmaps). We need to lock a Dedicated capacity plan that: 1) guarantees headroom for 95th percentile spikes, 2) lets us burst above reserved capacity for short windows without repeated manual intervention, and 3) has predictable billing for burst usage to satisfy procurement.

Questions we need Redwood to confirm:
- Proposed prewarm window (how far ahead should the preheating start for scheduled spikes?)
- Burst crediting model (do bursts consume reserved credits first, or are they billed as overage with monthly credit buckets?)
- Eviction priority during fleet contention (which customer tiers get preemption?)
- On-call/prewarm ops schedule and playbook for tenant-side triggers (we can provide scheduled ramp calendars)

Can you reply with a recommended prewarm matrix and a sample autoscale policy that maps our forecast bands to prewarm + burst behavior? Also share a short ops runbook we can include in the SLA appendix.

All — draft proposal below (high level). I focused on minimizing tail latency while keeping billing predictable. Happy to iterate.

Proposal: Prewarm + Burst crediting matrix (summary)
- Baseline reserved slab: sized to Blue Harbor 75th percentile steady demand (per spreadsheet).
- Scheduled prewarm (for predictable windows): start at T-20 minutes for medium spikes, T-45 minutes for >5x expected spikes. Preheat actions: allocate ephemeral GPU slots + KV cache priming for top-3 model shards; warm weights to NVCache. Expected warm time: 6–12 minutes depending on model size.
- Ad hoc prewarm (for unpredictable spikes): hold a small shoulder slab (2–4% of reserved) as instant preheat buffer that absorbs short spikes up to ~2–3 minutes.
- Burst pool & crediting: two-tier model
  * Credit bucket: monthly commit of burst credits (hours of burst at N GPUs) that are consumed first and priced at a discounted burst rate. Credits expire monthly and roll into a small carryover buffer (up to 10%) if unused.
  * Overage: if credits exhausted, bursts are billed at a higher overage rate but capped per spike (to avoid runaway invoices).
- Eviction & priority rules: production reserved capacity > credit-backed bursts > overage bursts. During contention, customers with reserved SLA (Gold) get preemption priority; credit-backed bursts are second; overage bursts are lowest priority and get evicted first.
- Autoscale policy (recommended):
  * Scaling steps: +25% -> +50% -> +100% of baseline with 60s evaluation window.
  * Cooldown: 5 minutes between steps; full cooldown to baseline 15 minutes after traffic drop.
  * Max burst duration per event: configurable (default 30 minutes) to limit cost exposure.
  * Canary: first 5 minutes of any new burst uses canary allocation to validate KV-hit ratios and tail latencies; auto-abort if P99 latency exceeds threshold.

Ops runbook (short):
- Trigger types: scheduled (calendar webhook), tenant-triggered via API, manual via ops console.
- Prewarm flow: schedule -> allocate ephemeral pool -> prime KV cache -> validate canary -> open full burst.
- Monitoring: token-level and GPU-util dashboards with automated alert to oncall at 60% predicted headroom consumption.
- Escalation: on persistent >30% overage for >60m, notify commercial & engineering.

Attachments: draft MOP stub attached for legal (contains the timeline and billing examples).

Action items:
- Jesse: confirm acceptable prewarm lead times and whether Blue Harbor wants monthly burst credits or prefers pay-as-you-go overage.
- Karthik/Marissa: I will produce a 1-page billing exemplar showing cost under both models.

-Vanessa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that layout looks sensible and pragmatic. A few clarifications from procurement:
1) We prefer a credit-bucket approach if the credits are charge-locked at a predictable blended rate (procurement hates variable spikes on their card). Can we provide a sample price band (we'll compare to our internal run cost).
2) For eviction, Blue Harbor will require a written guarantee that preemption events are limited to X per month for our reserved lanes; we can accept limited soft preemption on credit-backed bursts.
3) On the scheduled prewarm: T-45 for >5x is OK, but the engineering team would prefer a T-60 option for very large planned releases (they can give call times).

Procurement also asked for a short DocuSign addendum with the MOP + billing exemplar that they can sign along with the SOW. I've looped procurement on this thread.

Two items from our side: 
- I'll upload a revised spike calendar (weekly release dates) by EOD and link the DocuSign once ready.
- Please include a clause that limits overage cost per event to a % of monthly committed spend (this helps us with internal chargebacks).

Best,
Jesse
